newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia auctions exhibition hall, sets more sales.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia auctions exhibition hall, sets more sales.

text.p: Mongolia has auctioned an exhibition hall and a commercial centre in the capital, and will privatise at least 133 more buildings and shops by the year 2000, the state's Privatisation Centre said on Thursday.
The capital's 2,335 sq m exhibition hall was sold on Wednesday for 603.1 million tugriks ($757,000), compared with a minimum price of 441.1 million, the Privatisation Centre said.
The site was purchased by Gurvan Gol, a local company that conducts geological surveys.
A commercial building in the centre of the city with 1,467 sq m of space, was sold for 493.4 million tugriks to local food trading company Prestij, the Privatisation Centre said.
An 864 sq m shop, also in the city centre, produced no bidding interest and remained unsold. It carried a minimum price of 293 million tugriks.
By Thursday, 10 of the 27 commercial buildings scheduled for sale this month had already been sold.
The Privatisation Centre said at least another 133 buildings and shops in the capital but the schedule and minimum prices were being reviewed.
The list included six cinemas and several large shopping centres in the central area of the city.
The government was also preparing a list of state enterprises to be privatised, the Prime Minister's office said.
Prime Minister Mendsaikhanii Enkhsaikhan has recently said the yet unpublished list included Mongolian national airlines MIAT and the Gobi Cashmere factory, in the capital Ulan Bator.
